The study was conducted at the Eolos Wind Energy Research Station of the University of Minnesota, which has a 2.5 MW wind turbine and a 130 m meteorological tower.

The selected one-hour dataset was under a stable atmospheric condition with a mean hub-height wind speed of 7.8 m/s and a mean turbulence intensity ranging from 13% at the bottom tip to 5% at the top tip.
The blade root flapwise bending moment is about 10 times larger than the edgewise bending moment, indicating the flapwise moment dominates the structural response.

The blade root flapwise bending moment spectrum exhibits a clear peak at the rotor rotation frequency (1P = 0.22 Hz), in contrast to the foundation strain spectrum which peaks at the blade passing frequency (3P = 0.66 Hz).
The edgewise bending moment spectrum shows strong peaks at 0.97 Hz and 3.1 Hz, associated with the undamped natural frequency of the collective blade pitch control and its multiple.

The high-pressure and low-pressure surface strain spectra at the blade root match well with a slope of f^(-5/3) in the lower and intermediate frequency ranges, while the leading-edge and trailing-edge regions show significantly lower slopes.

The magnitude of the blade strain power spectrum increases with radial distance from the blade root, while the slopes of the power spectra decrease at outer radial positions in the intermediate frequency range.

The normalized fluctuation (standard deviation) of the flapwise bending moment exhibits clear periodicity at the rotor rotation frequency (1P), while the edgewise bending moment shows more fluctuations across the azimuth angles.
